name: Games in TypeScript | Retro Cabinet
tagline: A classic games platform where nine games share one engine contract, one game loop and one save system.
popTagline: A browser arcade of classic game clones.
popOverview: Originally built with Angular, it was rebuilt with Nutin to explore reusable gameplay systems and game architecture. Also, a perfectly legitimate excuse to play games during work hours.

sectionKeyPoints.Game registry: A single registry of games, from which routes and home page cards are built.

sectionKeyPoints.Typed options: Each game definition declares its settings (starting level, on/off options, etc) and a factory building the game from them.

sectionKeyPoints.Controls: Keys are handled by physical position, so QWERTY and AZERTY layouts both work.

sectionKeyPoints.A narrow contract: Every game implements reset, tick, key handling and optional snapshot / restore; the view drives it and renders a grid of cells or a canvas drawing.

sectionKeyPoints.One loop, two kinds of games: Grid games tick on chained timeouts that read their speed before every tick; canvas games tick on animation frames with a capped time step.

sectionKeyPoints.Defensive persistence: Stored data is treated as untrusted, and saves carry a version per game: older saves are dropped instead of being restored into the wrong shape.

sectionKeyPoints.Leaving the framework behind: RetroCabinet relied on Angular signals; making updates explicit moved logic out of the UI layer and into the games.

sectionKeyPoints.Real-time constraints: Game rules stay testable in isolation, away from rendering and timing.

sectionKeyPoints.Touch input: A D-pad, or a stick for steering games, sends the same key codes as the keyboard, so input stays a single concern for the games.
